subject: Checkout latency spike — action grid, mitigation plan, and customer update (draft)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example, jonas_weber@redwood.example
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [INVESTIGATE] P95 jump on checkout-gen (NimblePay, us-west-2)

Team —

Observed a sustained P95 increase (from ~420ms -> ~1.8s) on the generation API used by NimblePay's checkout flow beginning ~08:40 PDT. Affected requests are primarily long-context and variable prompt length (checkout histories + product lists). Key quick findings from the initial triage: 

- KV cache miss rate spiked for the NimblePay route (cache eviction window correlated with a small burst of 10k long-context sessions).
- Model scheduling shows a backlog on several GPU hosts serving the gen model; queue depth increased and batching window rose.
- No code deploys in the last 48h.

Immediate ask: we need product guidance on two emergency options we can flip now (both reversible):
1) Route NimblePay traffic to the dedicated low-latency pool (costly but short-term fix) — needs product/ops sign-off (estimated 5–10 min to flip).
2) Fall back to the smaller 8-bit quantized variant for checkout route for 60 minutes (reduces quality risk slightly but should restore p95) — needs product approval for quality tradeoff and customer notification.

Attached: grafana-checkout-p95-pre.png (snapshot at 09:05). Created INC ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3821.

Diego
SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.example, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example, jonas_weber@redwood.example
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: 2026-09-14T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [INVESTIGATE] P95 jump on checkout-gen (NimblePay, us-west-2)

Diego — thanks for the triage. Quick notes from infra side:

- We can flip routing to the dedicated pool immediately; risk is increased unit cost and potential slight reduction in global capacity. Rolling back is straightforward.
- Fallback to the quantized model is also feasible but requires a quick compatibility check for the current prompt schema (I can run a smoke test in ~7 minutes). Main risk: subtle tokenization shifts for multi-line receipts.
- Short-term alternative: enable a conservative batching window cap (cuts down the scheduling jitter) and persist prefix cache for the NimblePay route for 30m. That would be lowest risk and lower cost impact.

Proposed mitigation plan (ordered):
A) Persist prefix cache for NimblePay route (30m) — ~5m to enable.
B) If p95 > 1s after A, route to dedicated pool for 30–60m.
C) If throughput drops materially after B, fallback to quantized model as last resort and notify customer.

I will open a short-lived canary for the cache persist change (INF-3821-1). Need product approval to proceed with A and to prepare a customer-facing message in case we escalate to B/C.

-Karthik
Engineering (Serving Runtime)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, jonas_weber@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.example
Date: 2026-09-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: Customer update for NimblePay — please review

Team —

I drafted a short customer update for Lina/ops at NimblePay in case we need to move to routing/downgrade options. Please review tone and technical accuracy.

--- DRAFT ---
Subject: Brief update — addressing increased checkout latency

Hi Lina,

We identified a spike in latency affecting a subset of checkout requests this morning. Our SRE team is applying a short-term routing and cache-persistence change that we expect will restore normal response times within the next hour. If that does not fully resolve the issue, we may temporarily route your traffic to an alternative low-latency pool or switch to a slightly smaller model for a short window while we continue root-cause analysis.

What this means for you:
- We expect response time to improve within ~30–60 minutes.
- There may be a small reduction in throughput during a brief mitigation window; we will keep you informed and revert any change once stable.
- We will follow up with a post-incident summary and actions within 48 hours.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts checkout conversion. We are prioritizing this and will update you by 2:30 PM PDT or sooner.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Product
--- end draft ---

Edits requested: please add any clarifications for the fallback model behavior and confirm timing on the 2:30 PM update.

-Stephanie
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example, diego_fernandez@redwood.example
Date: 2026-09-14T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Customer update for NimblePay — please review

Steph — nice concise draft. A couple of tone edits and one ask: offer a small operational credit and explicitly name the contact to reach for urgent escalation. Suggested changes below (inline):

- Change: "We will follow up with a post-incident summary and actions within 48 hours." -> "We will send a post-incident summary within 48 hours and schedule a 30-minute review call if you'd like deeper technical context."
- Add: "We'd like to offer a one-time credit equivalent to two days of usage for the impacted route while we complete the postmortem."
- Add escalation contact: "For urgent issues please reach out to Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.example) or our SRE on-call."

If everyone is good, I'll send this from the CS mailbox and offer the credit; ask product to confirm.

-Marissa
Customer Success
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.example
Date: 2026-09-14T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Mitigation applied; p95 trending down — approval to send customer note

All —

Status update after mitigation steps A/B: 
- Step A (persist prefix cache) was enabled at 10:35 PDT and reduced initial jitter; p95 improved from ~1.8s -> ~900ms.
- We briefly routed a portion (~20%) of NimblePay traffic to the dedicated pool at 11:10 PDT to relieve queue pressure while cache persist warmed; p95 for that cohort dropped to ~420ms.
- After gradual rollback to normal routing at 12:05 PDT, overall p95 stabilized around ~520–650ms (still above baseline but acceptable for now).
- Current throughput is ~8% below the pre-incident baseline due to conservative scheduling knobs we left enabled; we are removing the temporary caps in a staged manner and expect throughput to return by EOD.

Attachments: grafana-checkout-p95-post.png (post-mitigation graph).

Approve sending the customer note as edited by Marissa (including the credit offer). Product sign-off: Stephanie, please confirm the 2:30 PM update window and the wording for the fallback model (we used the phrase "slightly smaller model with minimal quality impact").

Jonas
SRE (On-call)
